newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply off in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply off in thin trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished sharply lower, falling through key support areas as thin year-end volumes exaggerated the market's decline, dealers said on Wednesday.
Nikkei 225 March futures lost 320 points to close 10 points above their intra-day low of 20,075. Turnover was a light 12,505 lots.
"It's a thin December market. Prices between the buying and selling are far apart and it's easy to slip through the range," said a trader with a local institution.
He said 19,950-20,050 represented a critical support area for the March Nikkei after it broke through the 20,215 level.
A close below the support region would point to more weakness and possibly open the way for a drop towards 18,000 in the longer term, he said.

"Any good rally is still a sell on the New York front. And a big drop there could hurt the Japanese markets too," he said, adding that sentiment remained fragile on Wall Street despite Tuesday's 40-point rise.

He said news that Japan had registered an increase in its trade surplus for November, its first rise in two years, failed to boost the market as players felt the good news was already priced in and the Nikkei looked very weak technically.
